basis: Defining neurodevelopmental impairment; heart defects ~40-50%. Refractive disorders and otitis-related hearing loss are separate conditions; direct sensory damage >=30% is unproven.

decisions.ocular: none: common refractive errors and strabismus are separate diagnoses; direct sight-damaging lesions are not established in >=30%.
decisions.otologic: none: frequent hearing impairment largely reflects associated otitis/effusion; direct persistent ear injury in >=30% is not established.

basis: Asphyxiating skeletal dysplasia defines thoracic and pulmonary disease; cerebellar malformation and tongue hamartoma each 1/2. Renal anomaly frequency is unspecified.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy includes defining pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory insufficiency.

basis: Open neural and vertebral closure defect with Chiari II. Neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis; direct urinary tract injury in >=30% is not established.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder reflects spinal denervation and is separately diagnosed; direct urinary tract damage in >=30% is not established.

basis: Skin and oral mucosal keratoacanthomas define disease; ectropion causes eyelid dysfunction in 30-79%. Corneal complications are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral mucosal keratoacanthomas belong to the defining mucocutaneous neoplastic eruption; occasional dysphagia is not the basis.

basis: Generalized galactose metabolic defect; liver dysfunction, developmental impairment and cataracts are common, roughly >=30% each in small reported cohorts.

decisions.ocular: involved: cataracts are characteristic direct galactose-related lens injury in generalized GALE deficiency, approximately >=30%; reported cohorts are small.

basis: Thrombus occupies cranial venous channels; secondary brain edema, venous infarction or hemorrhagic injury occurs in roughly 40-60%. Headache alone does not qualify.

decisions.neurologic: involved: secondary brain injury occurs in roughly 40-60%; the defining lesion occupies venous sinuses rather than brain tissue.

basis: Mitochondrial disease defined by optic atrophy and/or auditory neuropathy; encephalopathy 3/3 and cortical atrophy 6/6 support neurologic involvement. Other findings lack reliable prevalence.

decisions.neurologic: involved: associated encephalopathy occurs in 3/3 and cortical atrophy in 6/6; the three primary slots retain metabolic and defining sensory axes.
decisions.otologic: primary: auditory neuropathy is explicitly part of the disease definition; its defining status supports inclusion despite unquantified frequency.

basis: Aromatase excess causes estrogen excess. Accelerated skeletal maturation occurs in 30-79% but does not itself establish bone damage; short stature is occasional (5-29%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: accelerated maturation alone is not destructive bone disease; persistent short stature is annotated in only 5-29%.

basis: Split spinal cord with myelomeningocele and vertebral dysraphism. Neurogenic bladder is a separate diagnosis; common direct urinary tract damage is not established for this subtype.

decisions.renal: none: extrapolated neurogenic bladder frequency does not establish direct urinary tract injury in >=30% of this rare subtype; bladder dysfunction is separately diagnosed.

basis: Lysosomal disease defined by developmental impairment and hearing loss; abdominal muscle hypoplasia is annotated in 80-99%. Recurrent infections alone do not establish immunodeficiency.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay is explicitly defining; intellectual disability and very frequent seizures reinforce neurologic disease.
decisions.otologic: primary: hearing loss is explicitly defining and annotated as very frequent (80-99%).
